The required synthesizable top module is adaptive_aero_control_top. Do not substitute a status, telemetry, register-bank, or leaf module as the design top. The top must implement the selected Physical AI application contract, external model request/response transport, validation, safety, timeout, and bounded actuator-command behavior.

EXTERNAL MODEL TRANSPORT DIRECTION CONTRACT (mandatory; this takes precedence over ambiguous ingress/egress wording in upstream prose): the RTL emits model-request valid/data as outputs and receives model-request ready as an input. The RTL receives model-response valid/data as inputs and emits model-response ready as an output. Apply this rule by data flow even when application-specific ports use cmd_*, req_*, rsp_*, or response_* names. A top-level output must have a real RTL driver; never connect a required top-level output only to a child input.

FIRMWARE CONTROL-PLANE CONTRACT (mandatory): this product journey requests generated firmware. The synthesizable top must expose a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with address, write-data, read-data, transaction-valid/write-enable, and response/ready semantics. DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.register_contract must describe the implemented registers and fields. Every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode; do not label inaccessible internal state as software-visible. The streaming transport may coexist with, but cannot replace, this interface.
Implement a synthesizable FPGA RTL top module named adaptive_aero_control_top. The design is a hardware command-and-safety wrapper for a remote GPU-executed automotive aerodynamics surrogate and must not implement the surrogate neural/network computation itself. The top module shall provide one inbound valid/ready stream (128-bit maximum) for compact command packets and one outbound valid/ready stream (64-bit maximum) for status packets. The design shall also expose a small memory-mapped CSR window no wider than 64 bits per access with address/data handshake sufficient to configure mode, watchdog timeout, actuator clamp limits, and fault clear. Command packets shall include, at minimum, a packet type field, sequence number, age or freshness field, operating-point summary for stream velocity, geometry descriptor/handle for DrivAerML STL reference geometry, desired actuator request, and integrity check field. The RTL shall parse packets, validate packet type, enforce the 20-55 m/s envelope, compare sequence numbers against the last accepted sequence, verify freshness against a programmable timeout threshold, and reject malformed packets. The design shall implement a watchdog timer that resets on accepted commands and forces safe fallback if the command stream is idle beyond the configured timeout. The safe fallback state shall drive actuator_cmd_out to a programmable safe position and deassert enable. All outgoing actuator commands shall be clamped between programmable minimum and maximum limits prior to driving outputs. Faults for stale command, timeout, checksum error, out-of-range input, and fallback active shall be latched and reportable through both the status stream and CSR window. The status packet shall include command acceptance/rejection, fault summary, current sequence tracking, fallback state, and clamped-output indication. The RTL shall be fully synthesizable, use only flip-flops and small control registers for state, and shall not infer large payload memories, tensor arrays, or flow-field storage. For FPGA implementation, use FPGA BRAM only if a bounded small FIFO or packet buffer is required, and do not instantiate any Sky130 macro. The design shall keep scalar-equivalent I/O below 256 pins by using streaming and CSR interfaces. Timing shall permit deterministic bounded-latency validation and fallback behavior at the target FPGA clock. The module shall be parameterizable for timeout count, clamp limits, and packet format version. The hardware/software partition assumes the onboard CPU/software performs any host-side interaction with the GPU worker or analytical reference, while the RTL is responsible for command transport, validation, watchdog, clamping, telemetry, and safe control enforcement.
FPGA MEMORY CONTRACT (mandatory): describe bulk payload/history/FIFO storage through a technology-neutral memory wrapper that the FPGA flow can map to native block RAM; do not flatten it into registers.
NO COMMAND FALLBACK CONTRACT (mandatory; overrides conflicting generated prose): do not create a fallback command, fallback register, fallback status, fallback controller, substitute command, or fallback-on-reset behavior. On invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions, inhibit/deassert actuator output validity and latch the fault for software handling. Do not silently replace the requested command.
